title: Design exercise: SAA-2.1-S02
scenario: Pinecrest Tutoring runs a live-lesson web tier that normally serves about 1,500 requests per second but reaches 4,000 every weekday when schools finish. The peak lasts about 60 minutes. The peak start differs by up to an hour between school terms but stays the same within a term, and the term dates are not tracked by anyone at Pinecrest. A new server needs roughly 10 minutes before it can take traffic, and in September students saw errors during the first 8 minutes of each peak. On top of the peak, unannounced surges of up to 30 percent occur whenever a teacher assigns a live quiz, and peak-sized capacity can be paid for during only a short window each weekday.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
There is no on-call rota, and engineers must not hand-edit timetables when school calendars change
Peak-sized capacity may be paid for at most 90 minutes per weekday in total, including warm-up time

rubric.label: Capacity is ready before each peak starts (allowing the 10-minute warm-up), with no hand-maintained calendar, and peak-sized capacity is held for no more than 90 minutes per weekday.
Unannounced 30 percent surges are absorbed with no manual action and without running peak capacity around the clock
